title: Robust measurement of Tofacitinib effectiveness for Ulcerative Colitis using health records
author: Vivek A Rudrapatna
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.2bqgamw
materials: Normal number of bowel movements for this patient
1 to 2 bowel movements more than normal
3 to 4 bowel movements more than normal
Obvious blood with stool most of the time
Mild disease -- erythema, decreased vascular pattern

steps.title: Identify Patient Diagnosis
steps.instruction: Determine if the patient has Ulcerative Colitis (UC), Crohn's Disease (CD), or NA.

substeps.instruction: Prioritize recent colonoscopy reports (indication, impression, and recommendations sections) near treatment initiation.
Alternatively, use the diagnosis from the GI encounter immediately preceding drug prescription.
Verify against the assessment and plan to avoid errors from EHR auto-population or copy-forwarded notes.

steps.title: Verify Tofacitinib Receipt and Initiation
steps.instruction: Confirm if the patient actually received Tofacitinib and if it was initiated specifically to treat IBD.

substeps.instruction: Check for patient messages, telephone encounters, or colonoscopy reports to confirm drug start dates.
Score 'Y' for initiation to treat UC; score 'N' if used for other conditions (e.g., rheumatological) or for steroid-sparing after subtotal colectomy.
Score 'Y' for patients with minimal endoscopic activity given treatment to improve symptoms.
Score 'NA' if the patient did not receive the medication.

steps.title: Assess Medication Use Consistency
steps.instruction: Determine if the patient took the medication regularly.

substeps.instruction: Annotate 'Y' if chart review shows irregular use due to personal preference or other reasons.
Annotate 'N' if no evidence of inconsistency exists.

steps.title: Record Patient Demographics
steps.instruction: Extract gender and disease onset details from the EHR.

substeps.instruction: Ascertain gender from clinic notes and demographic face sheet; score 'NA' if there is a mismatch or sex-change.
Determine Date of Disease Onset (YYYY-MM-DD) using the Notes tab, Scanned Clinical Documents, and Care Everywhere.
Round down to the 1st of the month or year if only those are known.
If only age of onset is known, select the first day of the next month following the birthdate (e.g., born 2/19/84, onset at age 10 = 3/1/94).
If symptom onset is unclear, use the date of colonoscopic diagnosis.

steps.title: Calculate Initiation Age and Disease Duration
steps.instruction: Calculate the patient's age and disease duration at the time of Tofacitinib initiation.

substeps.instruction: Calculate age in years (rounded down) using birthdate and initiation date; do not rely on copy-forwarded clinic notes.
Calculate disease duration in fractional years (months/12). For imprecise dates, use the earliest compatible day (e.g., '2 weeks prior' = 14 days).

steps.title: Determine Disease Extent at Initiation
steps.instruction: Categorize the anatomical extent of the disease prior to Tofacitinib initiation.

substeps.instruction: Use the following scale: 1 = Proctitis/Proctosigmoiditis; 2 = Left-sided colitis (up to splenic flexure); 3 = Extensive/pan-ulcerative colitis (beyond splenic flexure).
Prioritize sigmoidoscopic/colonoscopic data as the gold standard.
Use the maximum documented extent if findings are discrepant.
Data within 6 months of initiation is acceptable.

steps.title: Extract Baseline Mayo Scores and Labs
steps.instruction: Capture Mayo subscores and lab values within the 6-month window preceding Tofacitinib initiation (Month -6 to Month 0).

substeps.instruction: Stool Frequency: Score 0-3 based on increase over baseline. Define bowel movement as any trip to the toilet for blood, mucus, or feces. Impute baseline as 3 daily if not mentioned. Use the algorithm: closest to treatment failure, then closest to colonoscopy, then highest available.

Rectal Bleeding: Score 0-3. If severity is available: 0 (none), 3 (blood alone), 1.5 (vague/some), 1 or 2 (clear degree). If only frequency is available, use OCTAVE metrics. Use the most severe degree if multiple datapoints exist.
Physician Global Assessment (PGA): Score 0 (Normal/Remission), 1 (Mild), 2 (Moderate), 3 (Severe). Prioritize Assessment and Plan of clinic notes over insurance appeal letters.

Endoscopic Subscore: Score 0 (Normal/Inactive), 1 (Mild: erythema, decreased vascular pattern), 2 (Moderate: marked erythema, lack of vascularity, friability, erosions), 3 (Severe: spontaneous bleeding, ulceration). Use the most severely affected segment.
C-Reactive Protein (CRP): Use latest value in 6-month window. Report in mg/L. Report '0' if below quantifiable limit; report threshold if above.
Fecal Calprotectin: Use latest value in 6-month window. Report '0' if below quantifiable limit; report threshold if above.

steps.title: Review Treatment History
steps.instruction: Determine previous failures of other IBD therapies using clinic notes and global search.

substeps.instruction: TNF Antagonists: Identify use and failure of Infliximab, Adalimumab, Golimumab, or Certolizumab.
Oral Glucocorticoids: Identify failure of budesonide, prednisone, or prednisolone. Score as failure if patient was hospitalized and received IV steroids (e.g., methylprednisolone).
Immunosuppressants: Identify failure of Azathioprine, 6-Mercaptopurine, Methotrexate, Cyclosporine A, or Tacrolimus. Check thiopurine metabolite labs.

steps.title: Determine Tofacitinib Initiation and Censorship Dates
steps.instruction: Establish the precise timeline of drug use.

substeps.instruction: Initiation Date: Use patient messages or telephone encounters. If unavailable, use medication orders and round down to the 1st of the month/year. Prioritize the longest period of sustained use for on-off scenarios.
Last Known Use (Censorship Date): The last date the drug was observed being used (discontinuation, last clinic contact, surgery, death, or date of record review).

steps.title: Assign Censorship Status
steps.instruction: Categorize the status at the date of last use.

substeps.instruction: Score 1: Treatment deemed futile (lack of effectiveness, adverse outcome, or surgery due to failure).
Score 0: Administratively censored (still on drug at review, or discontinued due to insurance loss).
Score 2: Lost to follow-up (no IBD/treatment data for 1 year).
Score 3: Competing event (all-cause mortality).
Note: Surgery due to fibrostenotic strictures where drug was not resumed is scored as 0.

steps.title: Extract Follow-up Mayo Scores and Labs
steps.instruction: Capture data within the window of month 2 through month 8 after treatment initiation.

substeps.instruction: Stool Frequency, Rectal Bleeding, and PGA: Use the same scoring rubrics and selection algorithms as baseline.
Endoscopic Subscore: Use the modified Mayo scale (0-3). Select the latest datapoint up to the time of treatment failure. Exclude results confounded by superinfection (e.g., CMV).
C-Reactive Protein (CRP): Use latest value in 6-12 month window. Report in mg/L.
Fecal Calprotectin: Use latest value in 6-12 month window.

steps.title: Record Concurrent Therapies
steps.instruction: Identify other treatments that may confound Tofacitinib's effect.

substeps.instruction: Glucocorticoid Use: Mark '1' if patient received any systemic glucocorticoid (IV or oral Prednisone, Prednisolone, Budesonide) at follow-up. Exclude rectal steroids.

Other Co-therapy: Mark '1' for other IBD treatments (e.g., golimumab, vedolizumab, steroid enemas, 5-ASA, hyperbaric oxygen, VSL #3, curcumin) or systemic immunomodulators from other providers that reduce GI inflammation.
